finding: _remove_run_dir reads the registered worktrees with `_registered_worktrees(main_root) or {}`. When `git worktree list` fails at this point, the function sees no worktree, so it runs shutil.rmtree on the run folder even when a worktree that the ledger does not name is still in it. The check that keeps the folder exists for exactly that worktree, so a failed git call turns it off. The gap starts in the `or {}` fallback; cmd_close already stops on the same failure at its first call, so the fallback looks like an oversight. The smallest fix is in _remove_run_dir: when _registered_worktrees returns None, keep the folder and print an error that names it.
why_this_severity: cmd_close has already run `git worktree list` with success a moment before, so the second call fails only on a rare git error such as a lock or a full disk (no to fails_purpose). When it does fail, the close deletes the folder without the check, and a reader must know that the fallback opens the delete. The lines exist only on the story branch, so in_use is false.
